title: Lord! Deliver; Thou Canst Save
description: Lord! Deliver; Thou Canst Save in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Eliza Lee Cabot Follen wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 581, “Prayer for the Slave”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! de-liv-er; Thou canst save; Save from e-vil, Might-y God! Hear oh! hear the kneel-ing slave; Break oh! break th'op-pres-sor's rod.

lines: Lord! deliver; Thou canst save;
Save from evil, Mighty God!
Hear — oh! hear the kneeling slave;
Break — oh! break th' oppressor's rod.
May the captive's pleading fill
All the earth, and all the sky;
Every other voice be still,
While he pleads with God on high.
He, whose ear is everywhere,
Who doth silent sorrow see,
Will regard the captive's prayer,
Will from bondage set him free.
From the tyranny within,
Save Thy children, Lord! we pray;
Chains of iron, chains of sin,
Cast, forever cast away.
Love to man, and love to God,
Are the weapons of our war;
These can break th' oppressor's rod —
Burst the bonds that we abhor.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Eliza Lee Cabot Follen died in 1860.
credits: Words by Eliza Lee Cabot Follen (1787–1860), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
